steps.en: In a true parasternal long axis the beam cuts the basal septum and the posterior wall at right angles near the mitral leaflet tips, with the aortic root in line and the right ventricle lying above. All the linear measurements come from this one plane: cavity size at end diastole and end systole, septal and posterior wall thickness at end diastole, outflow tract diameter in mid systole, and aortic root diameters at end diastole. Measure on the two dimensional image rather than M mode whenever the beam is even slightly off axis, because an oblique cut overreads every distance it crosses.
Start at the left sternal edge in the third or fourth space with the marker toward the right shoulder, and slide or tilt until the apex points left and the aortic root opens fully.
Freeze an end diastolic frame at the onset of the QRS, where the cavity is largest, and an end systolic frame where the cavity is smallest.
Draw the cavity line perpendicular to the long axis at the level of the mitral leaflet tips, from septal endocardium to posterior endocardium.
Measure septal and posterior wall thickness on the same diastolic frame, keeping the line clear of right ventricular wall, trabeculation and chordae.
Zoom on the outflow tract and measure inner edge to inner edge in mid systole at the base of the aortic cusps.
Measure the aortic root at the annulus, the sinuses, the sinotubular junction and the ascending aorta on a diastolic frame, leading edge to leading edge.
Oblique cut through the ventricle. Fix: Rock the probe until the walls are brightest and the cavity is widest. An angled cut overreads wall thickness and distorts the cavity.
Wall thickness measured with trabeculation included. Fix: Stay on compact myocardium and keep the line out of the right ventricular wall, coarse trabeculation and chordae.

Outflow tract measured in diastole or outer to outer. Fix: Measure in mid systole from inner edge to inner edge, because the tract moves through the cycle and the valve area maths assumes the systolic orifice.
Aortic root measured at peak systole. Fix: Measure the sinuses, junction and ascending aorta at end diastole. Only the annulus is a systolic measurement.
Left ventricular internal diameter, end diastole. 42 to 58 mm in men, 38 to 52 mm in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular linear dimensions
Left ventricular internal diameter, end systole. 25 to 40 mm in men, 22 to 35 mm in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular linear dimensions
Septal and posterior wall thickness, end diastole. 6 to 10 mm in men, 6 to 9 mm in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular wall thickness
Left ventricular outflow tract diameter. Inner edge to inner edge in mid systole, usually about 18 to 22 mm in adults. Source: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis, section on outflow tract measurement

Aortic root at the sinuses, end diastole. About 34 mm in men and 30 mm in women, about 18 mm per sq m when indexed; leading edge to leading edge. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on the aortic root
M mode overreads when the beam is off axis, so prefer two dimensional lines for every number.
A basal septal bulge in older hearts can mimic hypertrophy, so measure wall thickness below the bulge.
A dilated root with an effaced junction still needs all four levels recorded and indexed to body size.

q.en: On which frame do you measure end diastolic cavity size and wall thickness?

o.en: At peak systole, where pressure is highest
At the onset of the QRS, where the cavity is largest
At the end of the T wave, where filling stops
At mid diastole, where the walls are still

why.en: End diastole is the frame of largest cavity volume, timed at the onset of the QRS. Measuring later in the cycle underreads the cavity and overreads relative wall thickness.

q.en: What is the correct convention for the outflow tract diameter used in valve area maths?

o.en: Outer edge to outer edge in end diastole
Leading edge to leading edge in end diastole
Inner edge to inner edge in mid systole
Inner edge to inner edge in end diastole

why.en: The continuity equation assumes the systolic orifice, so the outflow tract is measured inner edge to inner edge in mid systole at the base of the cusps.

q.en: What is the upper reference limit for end diastolic cavity size in men?

why.en: The ASE 2015 chamber quantification reference range for men runs 42 to 58 mm. Above this, consider dilatation and index to body surface area.

q.en: What is the timing and convention for aortic root diameters at the sinuses?

o.en: Mid systole, inner edge to inner edge
Peak systole, leading edge to leading edge
End diastole, inner edge to inner edge
End diastole, leading edge to leading edge

why.en: Root diameters are measured at end diastole with the leading edge to leading edge convention. Only the annulus is measured in systole.
